On 2005-06-08, Lance Armstrong finished fourth in the Dauphine Libere stage on Mont Ventoux and moved to second place overall, 21 seconds behind Levi Leipheimer.
On 2005-07-23, Lance Armstrong won the Tour de France for a record seventh time and retired from cycling.

On 2009-03-23, Lance Armstrong sustained a broken right collarbone during the opening stage of the Vuelta a Castilla y Leon in Spain and confirmed he would return to the United States for surgery later that week.
On 2012-08-23, Lance Armstrong was stripped of all seven Tour de France titles and banned for life from cycling after withdrawing his appeal against USADA doping allegations.

final_events.summary: Lance Armstrong spoke out against his former team Cofidis and others who would not take him on after his illness, following his Tour de France victory.
A letter cites Lance Armstrong, the Tour de France champion, as an example of someone whose fight against testicular cancer was made possible by chemotherapy.
Lance Armstrong won the 13th stage of the Tour de France and took the yellow jersey for the first time in that year's race.

Lance Armstrong denies using banned blood-booster erythropoietin or human growth hormone, while confirming he uses a permitted hypobaric chamber and saying he would re-evaluate his relationship with trainer Michele Ferrari if Ferrari is found guilty of supplying banned drugs.
Lance Armstrong won the fourth stage of the Tour de France, a 61-kilometre time trial from Montlucon, extending his overall lead with two stages remaining.
Lance Armstrong wins the Tour de France for the third time, finishing with a total time of 86 hours, 17 minutes and 28 seconds, six minutes and 44 seconds ahead of Jan Ullrich.
Lance Armstrong completed his first win of the season by winning the Midi Libre stage race in Southern France.
Lance Armstrong regained the yellow jersey and won the first mountain stage of the Tour de France, taking the overall lead.
Lance Armstrong announced he is likely to retire at the end of 2004, giving him two more attempts at the Tour de France.
Lance Armstrong and his wife Kristin confirmed they are to separate due to difficulty in their marriage.
Lance Armstrong competed in his first race of the year, the third stage of the Tour of Murcia, finishing in the main bunch.
Lance Armstrong avoided a crash by riding off the prescribed course into a field during stage nine of the Tour de France, and was not penalized despite breaking a rule against shortcuts.
Lance Armstrong acknowledged he is not as strong as in previous years and may lose the Tour de France, after struggling to defend his lead for a third consecutive day.
Lance Armstrong won Stage 15 of the Tour de France despite crashing during the climb of the Col du Tourmalet, increasing his overall lead over Jan Ullrich to one minute and seven seconds.

Lance Armstrong effectively secured his fifth consecutive Tour de France victory after Jan Ullrich crashed on a slippery roundabout during the final stage, extending Armstrong's overall lead to 1 minute 16 seconds.

Lance Armstrong's key mountain-stage teammate Roberto Heras is on the verge of leaving the US Postal team to join Spain's Liberty Seguros, potentially affecting Armstrong's attempt at a historic sixth Tour de France title.
Lance Armstrong finished 1 minute 6 seconds ahead of Jan Ullrich in a 21.3 km time-trial stage at the Tour of Murcia, their only head-to-head time-trial before the Tour de France.

Lance Armstrong confronts journalist David Walsh, co-author of an investigative book alleging doping, at a press conference on the eve of the Tour de France, and states he will pursue legal action over the book.
Lance Armstrong is competing in the Tour de France, seeking a record sixth victory, with Jan Ullrich as his most feared challenger.
Lance Armstrong won the 205-kilometre Pyrenean mountain stage of the Tour de France, moving closer to a record sixth Tour victory.
Lance Armstrong won stage 15 of the Tour de France and regained the yellow jersey, moving closer to a record sixth victory.
Lance Armstrong won the 15.5 km individual time trial to seize control of the Tour de France.
Lance Armstrong won the 17th stage of the Tour de France, retaining the overall lead and yellow jersey.
Lance Armstrong becomes the first man to win six consecutive Tour de France titles, from 1999 to 2004.
Lance Armstrong confirmed he will try to win a seventh Tour de France, possibly in 2006, and said he plans to decide in late April whether to attempt a seventh consecutive victory in July 2005.
Lance Armstrong confirmed he will attempt a seventh straight Tour de France victory.
Lance Armstrong is set to start Paris-Nice, his first major race of the cycling calendar, seven years after abandoning the event in 1998.
Lance Armstrong confirms he will attempt a seventh consecutive Tour de France victory in 2005, prioritizing it over the new ProTour series.
Lance Armstrong finished 24th in the Paris-Camembert single-day race, confirming his form ahead of the Tour of Flanders.

A former personal assistant to Lance Armstrong filed court papers in Austin, Texas, alleging he discovered a banned substance in Armstrong's apartment early last year, which Armstrong's attorney called false and absurd.
Lance Armstrong confirms that he will retire from professional cycling after the 2005 Tour de France, which will be his last race.
Lance Armstrong began the final countdown to the last Tour de France of his career by finishing fifth in the prologue time-trial of the Dauphiné Libéré, his principal preparation race.
Lance Armstrong finished fourth in the Dauphine Libere stage on Mont Ventoux and moved to second place overall, 21 seconds behind Levi Leipheimer.
Lance Armstrong fell during a training ride near Nice, sustaining a black eye, a cracked helmet, and road rash ahead of his attempt at a seventh Tour de France title.
Matt Damon is in talks to star in a film about Lance Armstrong, based on Armstrong's biography, with Damon reportedly Armstrong's preferred choice for the role.
Lance Armstrong will start his 10th and final Tour de France.
Lance Armstrong’s Discovery Channel team won the Tour de France team time trial stage, putting Armstrong in the yellow jersey for the first time that year.
Lance Armstrong reclaimed the yellow jersey after a strong ascent up Courchevel on stage 10 of the Tour de France, while most of his leading rivals were dropped.
Lance Armstrong retained the overall lead in the 2005 Tour de France after the 11th stage, won by Alexander Vinokourov, keeping the yellow jersey with a 38-second advantage.

Lance Armstrong effectively secured his seventh Tour de France victory, holding nearly three minutes over Ivan Basso after the final major mountain-top finish, with only the ceremonial final stage in Paris remaining.
Lance Armstrong wins the Tour de France for a record seventh time and retires from cycling.
Lance Armstrong secured his record-breaking seventh Tour de France victory in Paris, ending his cycling career.
Lance Armstrong denies allegations that he tested positive for a performance-enhancing drug in 1999, calling the claims a "witch hunt."
The article reflects on Lance Armstrong's retirement after his Tour de France victory, noting the retirement of his security vehicle, Air Force One.
Lance Armstrong admitted he is tempted to come out of retirement to bid for an eighth Tour de France win, saying he will no longer rule it out.
Independent investigators cleared Lance Armstrong of doping during the 1999 Tour de France, finding WADA and the French anti-doping lab committed misconduct.
The Sunday Times settled with Lance Armstrong and apologized after a court ruled its 2004 article implied he had taken performance-enhancing drugs.
Lance Armstrong returns to the Tour de France after nearly a year's absence, watching the race at L'Alpe d'Huez with actor Jake Gyllenhaal.
The IOC ethics commission rebuked WADA head Dick Pound for public comments about Lance Armstrong's alleged 1999 EPO use, a decision Armstrong called "a victory" after he had sought Pound's dismissal.
Lance Armstrong announced he intends to return to professional cycling and try to win an eighth Tour de France in 2009.
Tour de France organisers welcomed Lance Armstrong's plans to return to the 2009 event but warned he must adhere to stricter drug-testing regulations.
Speculation mounts that Lance Armstrong may return to competitive cycling in 2009, though Team Astana denies any contacts or plans to sign him.
Lance Armstrong confirms he intends to return to cycling and ride in the 2009 Tour de France.
Lance Armstrong confirmed he will begin his comeback to professional cycling in January with the Tour Down Under in Australia and join the Astana team.
Lance Armstrong confirms he will return to professional cycling in 2009, starting with the Tour Down Under in Australia and attempting to win an eighth Tour de France.
Lance Armstrong refuses to allow his 1999 Tour de France urine samples to be retested, rejecting the French anti-doping agency's invitation.
The International Cycling Union cleared Lance Armstrong to ride in the Tour Down Under in January, waiving the six-month advance registration rule.
Lance Armstrong agrees to compete in the Giro d'Italia for the first time in 2009 as part of his return to competitive cycling.
Lance Armstrong discusses doping allegations and his comeback in an interview, denying he used performance-enhancing drugs.
Lance Armstrong confirmed that he intends to ride in the 2009 Tour de France.
Lance Armstrong arrived in Australia ahead of his professional cycling comeback, saying he does not expect victory in the Tour Down Under.
Lance Armstrong trained in Adelaide heat in preparation for his competitive return with the Astana team at the Tour Down Under, which begins on 20 January.
Lance Armstrong is set to return to competitive cycling after three years in retirement at the Tour Down Under in Adelaide, where he will compete against 2006 Tour de France winner Oscar Pereiro.
Lance Armstrong launched the Livestrong Global Campaign at the Royal Adelaide Hospital, aiming to raise global awareness and action to conquer cancer.
Lance Armstrong attacked during the third stage of the Tour Down Under, escaped two major crashes, and was later caught after a furious chase.
Lance Armstrong admitted his return to competitive cycling at the Tour Down Under had been "disappointing" so far, sitting 38th overall, but refused to rule out a late victory surge.
Lance Armstrong backs Floyd Landis's return to professional cycling after Landis's two-year doping ban ends, saying people should "forgive and forget."

Lance Armstrong abandoned his proposal for an independent drug-testing programme supervised by Don Catlin due to logistical problems and high costs, instead using Ramsus Damsgaard for the Astana team's internal testing programme.
Lance Armstrong's one-of-a-kind time trial bike was stolen when thieves broke into his team's truck in Sacramento during the Tour of California.

Lance Armstrong, returning from retirement, helped Astana teammate Levi Leipheimer complete a Tour of California hat-trick, finishing seventh overall in his first race on home soil since coming out of retirement.

Lance Armstrong's Astana team confirms he will return to Europe to race in the Tour of Castilla y Leon, where he is set to race for the first time with teammate and rival Alberto Contador, and in the Milan-San Remo one-dayer.
Lance Armstrong returned to European racing at Milan-San Remo, where Mark Cavendish won.
Lance Armstrong tweeted praise for Mark Cavendish after Cavendish won the Milan-San Remo cycling race.
Lance Armstrong sustained a broken right collarbone during the opening stage of the Vuelta a Castilla y Leon in Spain and confirmed he would return to the United States for surgery later that week.
Lance Armstrong underwent successful surgery involving a five-inch stainless steel plate and 12 screws to repair a collarbone broken in four places after a racing accident on 2009-03-23.

The French Anti-Doping Agency said it is considering action against Lance Armstrong for allegedly failing to respect its rules during a March 17 out-of-competition test, potentially jeopardizing his Tour de France participation.
Lance Armstrong won the Nevada City Classic, his first victory since coming out of retirement, in his final race before returning to the Tour de France.
Lance Armstrong was competing in the Tour de France and remained in contention, with reports that he was talking about competing again the following year.
Lance Armstrong finished third in the 2009 Tour de France, behind winner Alberto Contador, and indicated he will most likely ride in the 2010 Tour de France.
Lance Armstrong said he is confident he can win an eighth Tour de France in 2010, while acknowledging Alberto Contador is very good and that he does not know if he will be good enough to beat him.
Lance Armstrong is expected to attend the 2010 Tour de France route announcement in Paris.
Lance Armstrong says he will retire from racing after the 2011 season.
Lance Armstrong tweeted "That was STRESSFUL!!" after crashes disrupted the first full stage of the Tour de France.
Lance Armstrong crashed at the foot of the Col de La Ramaz, effectively ending his chances of winning the Tour de France for an eighth time.

An unnamed cyclist corroborated claims that Lance Armstrong's former US Postal Service team engaged in systematic doping, supporting Floyd Landis's earlier allegations, while Armstrong continued to deny using performance-enhancing drugs.
Lance Armstrong faced new performance-enhancing drug allegations published in Sports Illustrated during the Tour Down Under, which he denied.
Lance Armstrong announced his retirement from professional cycling, which he described as "retirement 2.0" and is likely to be final.
Lance Armstrong faces new doping allegations, including testimony from former teammate Tyler Hamilton to a federal grand jury, which he denies.
The federal investigation into Lance Armstrong is abandoned after nearly two years.
The US Anti-Doping Agency formally charged Lance Armstrong and five associates with alleged doping violations, banning him from competition and potentially stripping his seven Tour de France titles.
Lance Armstrong was stripped of all seven of his Tour de France titles and banned for life from cycling after withdrawing his appeal against the US Anti-Doping Agency's doping allegations.
The US Anti-Doping Agency bans Lance Armstrong from competitive cycling for life and strips him of his seven Tour de France titles after he declines to challenge its doping investigation.
The US Anti-Doping Agency stripped Lance Armstrong of his seven Tour de France titles.
Livestrong Day, the cancer charity founded by Lance Armstrong, is held amid controversy over his doping conviction.
The US Anti-Doping Agency publishes a report detailing Lance Armstrong's doping practices and efforts to suppress the truth, leading to him being stripped of his seven Tour de France titles.

The UCI is reviewing USADA's reasoned decision that banned Lance Armstrong for life and stripped his titles, and will consider issues of appeal, jurisdiction, and statute of limitation within the 21-day appeal term.

The United States Anti-Doping Agency releases its "Reasoned Decision" detailing evidence of Lance Armstrong's use of performance-enhancing drugs and systematic doping by the US Postal Service and Discovery teams.

Eleven of Lance Armstrong's former teammates gave evidence against him to the United States Anti-Doping Agency, revealing what Usada described as a "doping conspiracy" at the US Postal Service Pro Cycling Team.

Following the US Anti-Doping Agency's release of evidence that Lance Armstrong used banned performance-enhancing drugs, an article questions whether his charity Livestrong should strip him of his chairman title.

Tour de France organiser Christian Prudhomme calls for Lance Armstrong's seven Tour de France victories to be erased and for no winner to be declared for 1999-2005, following a US Anti-Doping Agency report alleging systematic doping.
Bike-parts maker Sram terminated its product sponsorship agreement with Lance Armstrong, following Nike and other sponsors in abandoning him after the USADA doping report.
SCA Promotions is considering legal action to recover a $7.5m bonus paid to Lance Armstrong after he was stripped of his seven Tour de France titles.
The UCI accepted USADA’s verdict and stripped Lance Armstrong of his seven Tour de France titles, imposing a lifetime ban.

A commission headed by former appeal court judge Sir Philip Otton is announced to investigate the UCI's handling of the Lance Armstrong doping affair, with a wide-ranging remit including allegations made by Usada, the strength of the UCI's anti-doping measures, and payments Armstrong made to the UCI.
Greg LeMond, whose Tour de France titles were surpassed by Lance Armstrong, confirms he will run for the UCI presidency following the Usada report on systematic doping by Armstrong and associates.
Lance Armstrong confessed to doping in an interview with Oprah Winfrey.
Lance Armstrong is to give his first formal interview since being banned for life, with Oprah Winfrey, scheduled to be broadcast on 17 January 2013.
Lance Armstrong is set to give his first TV interview since the alleged doping scandal, choosing Oprah Winfrey for the appearance.
Lance Armstrong agrees to appear on Oprah Winfrey's show for a 90-minute interview, his first public remarks since being stripped of his Tour de France titles and receiving a lifetime ban for doping.
Lance Armstrong is due to give a public, televised confession to Oprah Winfrey regarding his use of drugs to enhance his cycling performance.
Lance Armstrong says he will answer Oprah Winfrey's questions directly, honestly and candidly in an upcoming televised interview, amid reports he will make a limited confession to doping.
Lance Armstrong admitted to taking banned performance-enhancing substances, including steroids and EPO, during his Oprah Winfrey interview.
Lance Armstrong apologized to Livestrong staff during an emotional meeting before his interview with Oprah Winfrey about doping allegations.
Lance Armstrong admitted his doping past in a televised interview with Oprah Winfrey, according to Winfrey.
The IOC stripped Lance Armstrong of his 2000 Sydney Olympics bronze medal in the time trial and disqualified him from the events in which he competed at the Games.

Lance Armstrong is scheduled to give his first interview since being stripped of his Tour de France titles and banned for life, a 90-minute special with Oprah Winfrey to be streamed live and broadcast in the US.
Lance Armstrong admitted to doping during an interview with Oprah Winfrey, opening him up to multiple multi-million dollar legal challenges.

Lance Armstrong confessed to using banned substances, including EPO, blood doping, testosterone, cortisone, and growth hormone, during all seven of his Tour de France wins in an interview with Oprah Winfrey.
Lance Armstrong admitted in an interview with Oprah Winfrey that he doped to win all seven of his Tour de France titles.
Lance Armstrong's first part of a two-part interview with Oprah Winfrey airs, in which he confesses to doping.
The UCI’s independent commission into the Lance Armstrong affair is to hold its first session to decide whether to include a truth and reconciliation process during its inquiry.
In an interview with Oprah Winfrey, Lance Armstrong admitted to doping and described himself as a bully and narcissistic.
SCA Promotions plans to file a lawsuit against Lance Armstrong seeking the return of $12m in performance bonuses paid for his 2002, 2003 and 2004 Tour de France victories after he admitted to doping.

JJ Abrams options the forthcoming book "Cycle of Lies: The Fall of Lance Armstrong" by Juliet Macur with the intention of turning it into a film, the first proposed movie announced since Armstrong admitted to blood doping and steroid use.
Lance Armstrong admitted in a televised interview with Oprah Winfrey that he had used banned, performance-enhancing drugs to cheat his way to a record seven Tour de France titles.
A lawsuit was filed by Rob Stutzman and Jonathan Wheeler accusing Lance Armstrong and his publishers of marketing his memoirs as true non-fiction despite later admissions of doping.
Armstrong's attorney says Armstrong has little expectation of having his life ban reduced or becoming eligible to compete in Olympic sports again.

Lance Armstrong could face criminal charges following his confessional interview with Oprah Winfrey, according to US media reports, though the US attorney's office said there was no active criminal investigation.
Lance Armstrong remains under active criminal investigation by US federal agents for obstruction, witness tampering, and intimidation, according to ABC News.
The US Justice Department joined a lawsuit against Lance Armstrong seeking to recover more than $30 million in US Postal Service sponsorship money.

A US Department of Justice court document raises the possibility that Lance Armstrong's former wife, Kristin, may be called to testify against him in Floyd Landis's whistleblower suit, alleging she witnessed Armstrong supplying doping products to Landis.
Lance Armstrong met face-to-face with whistleblower Emma O'Reilly in Florida, telling her his past attempts to ruin her reputation were "inexcusable and embarrassing."
Lance Armstrong was questioned under oath for the first time since his 2013 doping admission, in an arbitration case by SCA Promotions seeking to recoup $12 million in Tour de France bonuses.
Greg LeMond rejects calls for Lance Armstrong's life ban to be reduced, saying Armstrong deserves the ban for his doping and treatment of people.

The UCI’s Independent Commission on Reform in Cycling (CIRC) report is published, addressing how the Lance Armstrong era was allowed to happen and prompting further scrutiny of former UCI president Hein Verbruggen.

A report by cycling’s Independent Commission for Reform in Cycling found that the UCI colluded with Lance Armstrong from 1999 to 2009 to circumvent doping accusations and cement his status in the sport.
An arbitration panel orders Lance Armstrong and Tailwind Sports to pay $10 million in a fraud dispute with promotions company SCA.
Lance Armstrong returned to French roads to ride the "One Day Ahead" charity challenge with former footballer Geoff Thomas, raising money for CureLeukaemia, a day ahead of the Tour de France peloton.
A workmanlike biopic of disgraced doper and Tour de France cycling champ Lance Armstrong, titled The Program, is reviewed, featuring Ben Foster as Armstrong.
Lance Armstrong commented that Jan Ullrich would have been better off joining Team CSC for nothing rather than Coast, amid Ullrich's return to racing after a 14-month absence.
Lance Armstrong was rumored to be contemplating a comeback to professional cycling, though no comeback had occurred.
